WITH  MISC. APPEAL No. 1367 of 2009  DEVISINGH AND OTHERS  Versus  RADHAKISHAN AND OTHERS  Appearance:

Shri R.P. Gupta- Advocate for the appellants.
 Shri Nirendra Singh Tomar- Advocate for the Insurance Compan

ORDER Miscellaneous Appeal No.1304 of 2009 under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the impugned Award dated 16.07.2009 passed by the Fourth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.39/2008, primarily on the ground of alleged false involvement of the offending NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:430 2 MA-1304-2009 vehicle and seeking exoneration from liability.

Miscellaneous Appeal No.1367 of 2009 under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants-claimants challenging the same impugned Award on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

2. Since both the miscellaneous appeals arise out of the same Award passed by the Claims Tribunal and involve common questions of fact and law, they were heard together and are being decided by Devisingh vs Radhakishan on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113141645/
1 this common judgment.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 19.02.2008, the deceased Hari Singh, while returning from his relatives, reached A.B. Road, Dabha.

At that time, the driver of truck bearing registration No.
MP-06-HC-0271, by driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle of the deceased.
After causing the accident, the driver of the said truck fled from the spot along with the vehicle.
The incident was reported to the police.
FIR was registered and, after completion of investigation and other formalities, charge-sheet was filed before the competent Court.
Non-claimants No.1 and 2 were proceeded ex-parte before the Claims Tribunal.

The Insurance Company filed its reply denying the averments of the claim petition and specifically pleaded that, as per the Naksha Panchayatnama, the deceased died due to falling from his own motorcycle and that the insured vehicle was falsely implicated.
4. After framing the issues and appreciating the evidence adduced by the parties, the Claims Tribunal passed the impugned Award granting compensation in favour of the claimants.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:430 3 MA-1304-2009 5.
In MA No.1304/2009, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the impugned Award is contrary to law and facts available on record.

It was contended that the Claims Tribunal failed to appreciate the true scope of Sections 165 and 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which mandate that compensation can be awarded only when death arises out of the use of a motor vehicle.

It was further argued that the burden of proving involvement of the insured vehicle lay upon the claimants, which they failed to discharge, particularly in view of the delay of about one month in lodging the FIR against the insured vehicle.

Reliance was placed upon the Naksha Panchayatnama (Ex.P-7) and merg intimation (Ex.D-2), which allegedly indicate that the deceased died due to falling from his motorcycle, without involvement of the insured truck.
It was also contended that criminal case documents reflect false implication of the insured vehicle and that the seizure and immediate release of the vehicle indicate a pre-planned implication.
Learned counsel further submitted that only the mother of the deceased could be treated as a dependent and that the Tribunal erred in awarding compensation to other family members.
The income assessed and dependency calculated by the Tribunal were also challenged as excessive.
Hence, prayer was made for setting aside the impugned Award.
6. Learned counsel for the respondents/claimants opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of MA No.1304/2009.
7. Heard.

This Court shall first deal with MA No.1304/2009:-
8.

The appellant-Insurance Company has filed this appeal on the ground that in the Naksha Panchayatnama (Ex.P-7) it was mentioned that the death NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:430 4 MA-1304-2009 of the deceased occurred due to falling from the Devisingh vs Radhakishan on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113141645/
2 motorcycle.
Ex.P-7 reads as under:-

On the basis of Ex.P-7, it was argued that the death of the deceased did not occur due to the accident caused by the driver of the offending vehicle, but occurred due to the deceased himself falling from the motorcycle.

Reliance was placed upon the judgment of the Supreme Court in Insurance Company Limited v. Premlata Shukla and Others, reported in (2007) 13 SCC 476, to contend that when a document is exhibited by a party, such party cannot deny the contents of the document, and therefore the fact mentioned in Ex.P-7 was admissible and contradictory to the pleadings.

entities.text: Insurance Company Limited v. Premlata Shukla and Others, reported in (2007) 13 SCC 476
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. On perusal of the judgment in Premlata Shukla (supra), in the considered opinion of this Court,
the said verdict is not applicable to the present case, as in that case the document in question was an FIR lodged by the family members of the claimant.
In the present case, the Naksha Panchayatnama (Ex.P-7) was prepared by the Investigating Officer without any information given by the claimants.
It was the duty of the Insurance Company to examine the Investigating Officer to prove as to on what information such fact was mentioned in Ex.P-7.
The Investigating Officer was the best person to prove this fact.
However, by not examining the Investigating Officer, an adverse inference is drawn against the Insurance Company.
The Insurance Company also failed to examine any witness on whose information the Investigating Officer prepared Ex.P-7.

Therefore, the fact that the deceased died due to falling from the motorcycle was not duly NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:430 5 MA-1304-2009 proved by the appellant.
Accordingly, Ex.P-7 does not extend any assistance to the Insurance Company.
11. The merg intimation (Ex.D-2) is only information regarding an unnatural death, which sets the machinery in motion to enquire into the cause and manner of death.

After registration of Ex.D-2,
the police conducted enquiry, registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle, and after investigation, filed the charge-sheet against him.
12. The driver of the offending vehicle was proceeded ex parte before the Claims Tribunal and did not appear to rebut the evidence of the claimant witnesses and the criminal case documents.
Therefore, a presumption is drawn against him.

Though learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that Rajendra Singh (PW-3) is not a reliable witness and that he did not inform the police properly, upon consideration of his examination-in- chief, this Court finds that his testimony remained substantially unrebutted in cross-examination.

13. It is a settled principle of law that the evidence of eye-witnesses in motor accident claim cases is not to be tested with the same rigour as in criminal trials, and such evidence is to be appreciated on the principle of preponderance of probabilities and not proof beyond reasonable doubt.
14.
In the considered opinion of this Court, upon appreciation of the entire evidence on record, the testimony of PW-3 Rajendra Singh is reliable and inspires confidence.

The Insurance Company Devisingh vs Radhakishan on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113141645/
3 failed to examine the Investigating Officer to prove Ex.P-7, whereas PW-3 Rajendra Singh duly proved that the driver of the offending vehicle caused the accident.
This is not a case of false implication of the offending vehicle.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:430 6 MA-1304-2009 15.
With the aforesaid discussion, the MA No.1304/2009 filed by the appellant-Insurance Company is hereby dismissed.
Now, MA No.1367/2009 filed by the appellants/claimants is being considered:-
16. Learned counsel for the appellants-claimants submitted that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is inadequate.
It was contended that the deceased was working as a driver and his income ought to have been assessed as per the Minimum Wages Act.

It was further submitted that the Claims Tribunal erred in not awarding reasonable compensation under the heads of loss of consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses, future prospects, and in not applying the appropriate multiplier.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of compensation.
17. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of this appeal.

18. Heard.
19.

On perusal of the impugned Award and the evidence available on record, this Court finds that the monthly income of the deceased as assessed by the Claims Tribunal at Rs.3,000/- is based on the material on record and does not call for interference.

20. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 40% and as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:430 7 MA-1304-2009 6 SCC 121

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 16 should be applied and 1/2 personal expenses of deceased should be deducted as he was bachelor at the time of the accident.

21. Accordingly, appellants-claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT  Income Rs.3000X 12= 36000 p  After adding Future Prospects@40% Rs.50400/-
 After Dependency1/2 Rs.25200/-
 Loss of Income Rs.25200 X 16=403200  Loss of consortium Rs.40000 X 2 = 80000  Other Heads:- Rs.30000/-
Devisingh vs Radhakishan on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113141645/
4  Total Compensation = Rs.
22.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.5,13,200/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs. 1,55,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.3,58,200/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
23. In the result, MA No.1367/2009 is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.3,58,200/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:430 8 MA-1304-2009 remain intact.

24. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants-claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
25. In view of the foregoing discussion and analysis, Miscellaneous Appeal No.1304/2009 filed by the Insurance Company is found to be devoid of merit and is dismissed.
Miscellaneous Appeal No.1367/2009 preferred by the appellants/claimants
succeeds partly and is hereby allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove.

26. Let a copy of this order be placed in the record of the connected MA No.1367/2009.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
